DATA & TRUST

A clear view
of what stays where.

The public site explains the project. The browser demo illustrates one garment comparison. Your own application workspace is a separate installation.

The public website.

This website serves static HTML, CSS, JavaScript and licensed garment photographs. Project Crumble does not add analytics, advertising pixels, account registration or contact-form collection to these pages. Fonts and images are served with the site.

The hosting provider handles requests needed to deliver the site and may keep service or access logs under its own policies. Visiting GitHub or another linked site is governed by that service's policies.

The browser demonstration.

The design change lab uses real garment photographs with manual observations and a separate hypothetical operation-time scenario. It does not upload photographs, call a model or send review data to an application server.

  • Choosing a photo changes the garment comparison. Sleeve and pocket controls update a separate in-browser calculation; they do not alter the real photographs.
  • “Save draft” writes your choices, optional reviewer name and note to this browser's local storage on this site's origin.
  • “Restore saved draft” reads that local record. “Clear saved draft” removes it.
  • “Download review JSON” creates a file on your device. It does not submit your review to the project.
  • “Reset example” restores the on-screen example. It does not delete a saved draft; use “Clear saved draft” for that.

Other people with access to the same browser profile may see a saved draft. Do not put confidential factory or customer information in a public demonstration. Browser site-data controls can also remove local storage.

Your installed workspace.

The open-source application runs wherever you install it. Your garment records, imported image derivatives, embeddings, evidence snapshots and reviews are stored in its configured workspace. They are not uploaded to this public website.

If you configure a remote host, model provider or future external integration, review the data path and that service's terms. Downloading public model files also makes requests to the model hosting service. The project does not ship private retailer datasets or credentials.

You control access, backups, retention and deployment. The alpha's reviewer names are attribution fields, not verified accounts. Read the deployment guide before exposing an application beyond your machine.

Real photographs & credits.

The four garment photographs were published by Reistor on Unsplash. Their source pages list camera metadata and the Unsplash License, which permits commercial and non-commercial use. We resized and converted the photographs to WebP; page layouts may crop them. We did not generate or change the garments.

  • Beige hemp dress / front view — Reistor. Published 2025-05-16.
  • Off-white hemp shirt / construction detail — Reistor. Published 2025-07-18.
  • Blue floral dress / reclining view — Reistor. Published 2025-06-13.
  • Striped dress / back detail and homepage hero — Reistor. Published 2025-06-13.

The garment names come from the source descriptions. Visible details are manually reviewed photo observations, not model output. A detail outside a photo's view remains unknown. These separate garments do not establish copying, chronology or brand influence. Reistor is credited as the photo source, not presented as a Crumble customer or sponsor.

Photo rights remain under the Unsplash License. Apache-2.0 covers the project code, not these photographs. See the photo source manifest and repository third-party notices. Scenario operation times are invented examples, not factory standards.

Questions or security concerns.

Use the repository's security policy for private vulnerability reporting. General project questions can be raised through GitHub issues. Keep private garment data, credentials and customer information out of public reports.
